newsitem.title: UK: UK blocks Bass merger with Carlsberg-Tetley.
newsitem.headline: UK blocks Bass merger with Carlsberg-Tetley.

text.p: The UK government said on Friday that it was blocking the planned merger between brewing to hotels group Bass Plc and Carlsberg-Tetley, a deal that would have created Britain's largest brewer.

Margaret Beckett, recently appointed Labour's trade and industry minister, said that she did not agree with the view from the Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC) that the adverse effects of the merger could be adequately addressed by the sale of around 1,900 Bass pubs.
The government also said that it was to seek an undertaking from Bass that it would sell its existing 50 percent stake in Carlsberg-Tetley.
"I am not persuaded that the divestment of 1,900 pubs would be an adequate counterweight to the substantial strengthening of Bass's position as a producer and wholesaler of beer," said Beckett.

"Bass's acquisition of Carlsberg-Tetley would represent would represent a further substantial step in the direction of concentration in an industry which has already seen the number of national brewers with tied estates fall from six to four since 1989," said Beckett in a statement.
Brewers in Britain are allowed to operate a so-called tie system whereby the pubs it owns are obliged to stock only beers it brews.
Approval of the deal would have allowed Bass, which has an estimated 23 percent of the market, to leapfrog Scottish & Newcastle Plc which sells 29 in every 100 pints consumed.

Under the deal struck last August, Bass paid 200 million pounds ($333.1 million) for the 50 percent interest in Carlberg-Tetley owned by drinks group Allied Domecq. Carlsberg, the Danish brewer that held the rest, agreed to contribute its interest to Bass together with 20 million pounds, in exchange for 20 percent of the merged business.
